hardware.candidate_role: USB/display signer overlong serial recovery smoke
hardware.tested_state: existing flashed firmware with updated hardware smoke script

procedure: Extended idf-smoke-capabilities so the shared overlong serial-frame vector is immediately followed by a valid get_capabilities request using request_id post-overlong-recovery.
Ran nSealr/esp32 make ci with Python tests, host-core tests, compileall, and firmware validation.
Exported ESP-IDF v5.5.4 from /Users/vincenzo/esp/esp-idf-v5.5.4/export.sh in the same shell invocation used for hardware smoke.
Verified idf.py, esptool.py, ESP-IDF v5.5.4, and /dev/cu.usbmodem1101 before opening the board port.
Ran make IDF_PORT=/dev/cu.usbmodem1101 idf-smoke-capabilities against the existing flashed firmware image.
expected_result: The attached board rejects malformed serial transport deterministically, reports overlong_frame for the oversized transport vector, drains the rejected line, then accepts the immediately following post-overlong-recovery capability request while keeping sign_event at signing_disabled.
observed_result: The hardware smoke passed with 39 USB serial exchanges: 9 response frames and 30 expected rejection frames. The added post-overlong-recovery request received a valid response after the overlong_frame rejection. Valid sign_event requests still returned signing_disabled, invalid signing requests returned unsupported_request, and malformed transport vectors returned malformed_frame or overlong_frame.
limitations: This is protocol smoke using the existing flashed firmware image; it is not a new build or flash report.
This is not a new manual visual display inspection.

The run does not validate production trusted-display acceptance, production physical-control acceptance, key provisioning, storage, secure boot, flash encryption, debug lock, companion signed-output verification, or real signing.
sign_event is expected to remain signing_disabled until every production signing gate is satisfied.
